PERSONAL / SOFTGOODS / CASE STUDY 10

Inseam-Panel Flared Jeans

Add volume through the inseams to create a wider lower-leg silhouette while preserving the outside seam line.

Project type
Personal project
Role
Designer & Maker
Timeline
2024–2025
Exact completion month was not recorded.
Disciplines

Status
Completed
01 Problem02 Requirements03 Concepts04 Pattern Geometry05 Design06 Build / Test07 Results08 What I Learned
01

Problem

For this pair, I added material at the inseams instead of the outseams to change where the lower-leg volume developed.

The goal was to widen the silhouette using donor denim while keeping the existing upper garment.

02

Requirements

RequirementEngineering definition
Base garmentReuse an existing pair of jeans.
Panel placementOne inseam insert per leg.
Seam allowance0.5 in.
FitBalance the added width between the legs.
03

Concepts

ITERATION / 01

Compare the base silhouette

Lay out the original garment to identify where the inseam should be opened.

ITERATION / 02

Introduce tapered volume

Use triangular inserts to transition from the original leg into a wider hem.

04

Pattern Geometry

Pattern dimensions below are estimates; seam allowance is 0.5 in.

Finished insert geometry: 14 in height and 4 in width at the hem seam line. Starting from an 8 in laid-flat opening (16 in circumference), one 4 in panel per leg increases the finished laid-flat width to approximately 10 in (20 in circumference).

Offset both sloping stitch lines and the hem by 0.5 in. The mitered cut outline is approximately 5.15 in wide and 18.04 in high. Truncate the sharp tip as needed for construction.

05

Design

The inseam panel increases the available fabric toward the hem while retaining the garment’s outside seam.

Matching the two inserts helps the added volume read consistently when the jeans are worn.

06

Build / Test

The photographs show the original silhouette, the opened inseams with insert material positioned, and the finished jeans.

07

Results

The finished jeans show a wider lower-leg silhouette created through inseam inserts.

2inseam inserts, one per leg
0.5 inseam allowance
Reusedbase garment and donor denim
08

What I Learned

Moving an insert from the outseam to the inseam changes the way added fabric is distributed. Comparing both approaches helped me think about silhouette as a pattern-design problem.
